newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-HENMAN-MANIA CAUSES BOOKIES TO CUT ODDS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-HENMAN-MANIA CAUSES BOOKIES TO CUT ODDS.

text.p: Tim Henman's superb start to 1997 led British bookmakers to cut his odds on winning the Australian Open to 16-1 on Monday, and they said they faced a huge payout if the Briton won a grand slam tournament this year.
Ladbrokes said Henman was priced at 66-1 to win the first grand slam event of the year at the beginning of last week, but his victory in a Sydney warm-up tournament saw his odds cut to 25-1.
Sydney gave Henman the first title of his career after he reached the final in Doha earlier in the month.
"Tim continues to attract fantastic interest among the British betting public," Ladbrokes spokesman Ian Wassell said.
"He is playing at the top of his form and with Boris Becker out it seems to us that only Michael Chang provides a major obstacle to Henman reaching his first grand slam final."
Becker was beaten in the first round by Spain's Carlos Moya on Monday.
"We already face a 100,000 pound ($168,000) payout if Henman wins the Australian Open and I dread to think what it would cost if he were to win Wimbledon," Wassell said.
